title: The Loire
subtitle: Europe's longest wine valley
objectives: Describe the Loire's four main areas
Explain why Loire wines are fresh

steps.title: Four areas
steps.body: The Loire runs about 1,000 km, with vineyards along much of it. Near the Atlantic, the Pays Nantais makes Muscadet from Melon. Anjou-Saumur makes Chenin Blanc, from dry to sweet, and Cabernet Franc. Touraine makes Vouvray Chenin and Chinon Cabernet Franc. Upstream, the Central Vineyards make Sancerre and Pouilly-Fumé from Sauvignon Blanc.

steps.title: Cool and fresh
steps.body: The Loire is at the northern edge for many grapes. The west is maritime; the Centre is more continental. Cool conditions keep acidity high and alcohol moderate, often 11.5 to 13%. That freshness explains its whites, its sweet wines that never cloy and its sparkling Crémant de Loire and Saumur.

steps.prompt: Match each Loire wine to its grape.
steps.explanation: Each part of the Loire has its own grape.

steps.body: Muscadet sur lie, aged on its lees until bottling, is one of the most reliable partners for oysters, and one of France's best bargains.

steps.prompt: Why do Loire wines tend to have high acidity?
steps.explanation: The Loire is cool, so grapes ripen slowly and keep their acidity.

steps.title: What you learned
points: The Loire has four areas, from Nantais to the Centre
Melon, Chenin Blanc, Cabernet Franc and Sauvignon Blanc lead
A cool climate keeps the wines fresh
